subject: Error in LDpred2 due to different human genome builds for different summary summary stats

messages.author: 9600a7a9e426959d
messages.subject: Error in LDpred2 due to different human genome builds for different summary summary stats
parts:
Hello, 

I am using two different hg builds (hg38 and hg19) for 6 traits for commonfactorGWAS. Though I could successfully obtain 1-factor GWAS sumstats, but to derive polygenic risk scores based on this 1-factor GWAS summary statistics, LDpred2 gives an error as I have used two different hg builds to construct sumstats. Is there a way where I can harmonize after the common factor GWAS step to circumvent the error in LDpred2?

Thanks in advance for any inputs.

Best Regards,
Rajini

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Combining summary summary stats from different human genome builds
parts:
Hi Rajini, 

Thanks for following up about this (there are period when these posts get lost in the hectic period of the semester so the lack of response had nothing to do with the question itself as I think it's a great one). 

The relevance of the genome builds will likely depend a bit on the level of analysis you are conducting. If you are strictly running genome-wide models, since those only use the LDSC genetic covariance matrices, which are themselves estimated only using common HapMap3 SNPs that are unlikely to shift across builds, I would not anticipate that the build matters. If you are running multivariate GWAS (as it sounds like you are), I would say that it is still not a huge cause for concern as only a small subset of SNPs are likely to both pass QC and listwise deletion that would shift across builds. 

With that said, if a software like LDpred is requiring that you use a particular build, or you want to be extra sure that genome builds are not affecting results, there are a number of options out there, but one of the more accessible and easy to use packages that I've found is one in R called MungeSumstats that includes a liftover function that could be used to align all input summary stats to the same build prior to running the sumstats function in Genomic SEM, or to convert the multivariate GWAS summary stats to a particular build. Example code that could be run in R below to convert from build 37 to 38 could be written as:

library(MungeSumstats)

sumstats38 <- MungeSumstats::liftover(sumstats_dt = sumstats37, ref_genome = "GRCh37", convert_ref_genome = "GRCh38", start_col = "BP", end_col = "BP") 

Best, 
  Andrew
